questions.q: Describe the achievements of the Kushanas under Kanishka.
answer: The Kushanas ruled a vast territory stretching from Central Asia into north India, and reached their height under Kanishka in the first and second centuries CE.

answer.text: Kanishka supported Buddhism, is associated with a Buddhist council, and under his rule Buddhism spread along the Silk Route into Central Asia and China.

Two great schools of sculpture flourished — the Gandhara school, which showed Greek influence, and the Mathura school, which was indigenous. Both produced some of the earliest images of the Buddha in human form.
The Kushanas controlled key trade routes and issued fine gold coins, making their empire prosperous and cosmopolitan.

questions.q: What do we know about the Sangam Age of the Tamil south?
answer: The far south during this period is known as the Sangam Age, after its remarkable literature.

answer.text: Tamilakam was ruled by three dynasties — the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas, together called the muvendar or three crowned kings.

Our main source is Sangam literature, early Tamil poetry composed in assemblies (sangams) traditionally held at Madurai, the Pandya capital. It vividly describes kings, warfare, love, trade and daily life.

The region carried on a brisk trade with the Roman world, exporting pepper and spices; Roman coins found in the south and the account in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea confirm this flourishing commerce.

questions.q: Describe the Satavahana dynasty of the Deccan.

answer.text: After the Mauryas, the Satavahanas rose to power in the Deccan and western India and ruled for several centuries. Their greatest king was Gautamiputra Satakarni, who extended the kingdom and defeated rival powers.
The Satavahana kings took proud titles, and inscriptions record their conquests and gifts. Some queens, such as Gautami Balashri, were prominent, and the dynasty is notable for its royal women.

Under the Satavahanas, trade flourished, both within India and by sea with the Roman world, bringing prosperity. They patronised Buddhism, and beautiful stupas and cave monasteries were built in their realm.

answer: Thus the Satavahanas were a powerful Deccan dynasty known for strong kings, flourishing trade and support for Buddhist art.

questions.q: How did trade and contact with other lands grow in the period after the Mauryas?

answer.text: The centuries after the Mauryas saw a great expansion of trade, both overland and by sea. Goods moved along routes such as the Silk Route, and ports on the western and eastern coasts handled busy overseas trade.

Indian merchants traded with Central Asia, China, Southeast Asia and the Roman Empire. India exported spices, fine cotton and silk cloth, ivory and precious stones, and received gold, wine and other goods in return, so that Roman gold coins have been found in the south.
Along with goods travelled people, ideas and religions, so that Buddhism spread to Central Asia and beyond.

answer: Thus flourishing overland and sea trade linked India with distant lands and carried its goods and ideas across the world.
